## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A one-fascicle Tang revision of the **Eleven-Faced Avalokiteśvara** dhāraṇī-sūtra by **Xuánzàng** ([玄奘](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%A5%98), 602–664), the Faxiang patriarch and the most consequential Sanskrit-to-Chinese translator in Chinese Buddhist history. The text is Xuánzàng's reworking of the older *Ekādaśa-mukha* sūtra previously translated under the Northern Zhōu by [耶舍崛多](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%80%B6%E8%88%8D%E5%B4%9B%E5%A4%9A) ([KR6j0276](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0276) = T20n1070).

**Abstract**

The sūtra opens at Veṇuvanaviṃśopa-vāstavya (室羅筏竹笋道場) with the assembly of 1,250 *bhikṣus* and innumerable bodhisattvas led by Maitreya. Avalokiteśvara then announces and discloses the **Ekādaśa-mukha-dhāraṇī**. Compared to Yaśogupta's earlier rendering ([KR6j0276](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0276)), Xuánzàng's text is rhetorically more polished, the Sanskrit transliteration more rigorous, and the narrative frame slightly expanded — characteristic markers of the Cí'ēnsì 慈恩寺 translation bureau's mid-seventh-century method. The *xīnjīng* (heart-sūtra) framing in the title is generic for *hṛdaya-dhāraṇī*-genre texts and does not refer to the *Prajñāpāramitā-hṛdaya*. Xuánzàng's recension circulated alongside Yaśogupta's older version and they were later both supplemented by [不空](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%B8%8D%E7%A9%BA) Amoghavajra's full *yíguǐ* manual ([KR6j0275](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0275) = T20n1069). CANWWW (T20N1071) cross-references [KR6j0276](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0276) (T20N1070) and the Atikūṭa compendium ([KR6c0098](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0098), T901).
